I’ll trace the broadcast lifecycle and scheduling API, then make the smallest backend/UI change needed. I’ll avoid dependency installation and test execution as requested.
I found the failure path: audience edits intentionally pause an existing schedule, while the relaunch flow only adds another schedule and leaves prior schedule state unmanaged. I’m using the frontend conventions and copy guidance before adding the draft action and replacing schedules on launch.
The UI will expose an “Edit broadcast” action only while the live broadcast has not started a batch run. It returns the flow to draft, where its existing values are already hydrated for editing. On launch, I’ll fetch and delete every attached schedule, then create one new active schedule for the selected time; immediate sends clear old schedules as well.
The implementation is in place. I also ensure the in-memory broadcast reflects the replacement schedule, so the summary can immediately offer editing after a scheduled launch, while immediate sends do not retain a stale schedule.
Implemented the broadcast lifecycle change.

- Added an **Edit broadcast** action for active scheduled broadcasts with no started run. It moves the broadcast back to draft so it can be edited.
- Relaunching now deletes all existing schedules before activation, then creates one fresh active schedule for the selected time. Immediate sends also clear stale schedules.
- Kept the summary state synchronized with the newly created schedule.
